newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE maize futures ease, milling wheat up.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE maize futures ease, milling wheat up.

text.p: Old (1996) crop maize futures prices dropped on the Budapest Commodity Exchange grain section while wheat price rose for all maturities, traders said on Monday.
"Maize export outlooks remain bleak and the surplus is still there," said Istvan Grebats of Termin Broker.
He added that there were only few potential buyers in the region and Romania also had some surplus.
"Poland could be one of the export markets, but US maize can sometimes be cheaper for them," Grebats said.
Better financing and cheaper shipment are the main advantages of US maize, he added.
Maize prices ended at 19,250 forints for March, down 100, 19,080 for May and 18,950 for July, both down 150.

Milling wheat prices rose by the maximum allowed daily change of 400 forints for all deliveries but there was room for further rises as the Central Statistical Office's estimate of 3.9 million tonnes 1996 crop might have been too optimistic, Grebats said.
However, most prices remained speculative and woIuld only show a more realistic picture as delivery dates were within sight, he added.
Milling wheat prices ended between 29,040 forints for March to 24,100 for December.
Monday's total turnover was 456.1 million forints or 1,140 contracts, of which 974 contracts were for maize.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
